idiom_name: suspend enrich function; async/awaitAll for parallel lookups; Flow.map for streams
implementation_notes: Kotlin's coroutines reduce the enricher to a suspend function: read the key, await the resource (client or repository) and return a copy with the missing fields - no Enricher class, no thread per message. Independent lookups for one message run concurrently with async/awaitAll inside a coroutineScope, and when messages form a stream, Flow.map (or mapLatest/transform) applies enrichment as an operator that keeps backpressure; caching is a ConcurrentHashMap, Caffeine or an explicit Flow-level deduplication. The data source stays an interface so tests inject a fake.
pitfalls: getOrPut on a plain HashMap is not thread-safe; use ConcurrentHashMap.computeIfAbsent or a Caffeine cache for concurrent consumers.
A suspend lookup inside map keeps ordering and backpressure but serialises the lookups; add buffering or an async/mapAsync-style stage when the resource can handle parallelism.
Cancellation must reach the resource client, otherwise a cancelled message still completes its lookup and may write to a cache nobody will read.
